bodies.name: nut
bodies.note: inertia about the COM in the body frame; explicit, never recomputed from the OBJ

joints.name: nut_drive
joints.note: X_p / X_c = x y z qx qy qz qw; FREE: 6 undriven DOF; D6: the listed DOF only, all others locked

drive.kind: joint drive on nut_drive (a D6: the axial slide and the spin about the bolt axis +z)
drive.axial: constant joint force -5 N on the slide from t = 0 (opposes the advance)
drive.spin: velocity drive, kd = 10 N m s/rad, target omega(t) = 3.14159265 rad/s * smoothstep(t / 0.1 s), smoothstep(s) = s^2 (3 - 2 s) on [0, 1]; t = k dt over step k; implicit (MuJoCo implicitfast velocity actuator), effort limit as in joints

arrays.joint_f: [steps, W, 2] float32: feed-forward joint force (slide N, spin N m) over step k
arrays.target_qd: [steps, W] float32: the spin drive's target velocity (rad/s) over step k

alloy_collision.representation: analytic: the bolt's ISO thread SDF (no voxels, no texture) against samples on the nut's thread flanks; the MuJoCo cylinders 'bolt' / 'nut' are filtered from collision
alloy_collision.nut_samples: 5e-05 m grid on the middle 20% of each flank, from 0.5 pitch inside each nut face, 12 sectors
alloy_collision.pack_meshes: thread_sdf.thread_mesh, 96 segments per turn; bolt cut to (-0.01, 0.01) m (Alloy's analytic bolt: (-0.025, 0.025) m)

engine_collision: Load each OBJ as a triangle mesh with the engine's own mesh-SDF collision at its documented recommended settings for the scene type; record the SDF resolution / spacing, contact offsets / margins and their sources in meta.settings. Do not re-hull, decimate or decompose. A static part may use the engine's static triangle-mesh path if its SDF contact needs that (say so). Only the listed contact pair collides.

export.frames: a frame every physics step (record_every 1), frame 0 the initial state; W axis = cond.json worlds

channels.body_q: [T, W, B, 7] float32: body origin + quaternion x y z w, world frame (contract)
channels.body_qd: [T, W, B, 6] float32: COM linear + angular velocity, world frame (contract)
channels.joint_q: [T, W, 2] float64, optional: the nut's axial position z (m) and spin angle theta (rad) about the bolt axis +z, continuous (unwrapped; theta grows as the nut runs down). Without it, z and theta come from body_q (Newton eval_ik, theta unwrapped over frames)
channels.drive_tau: [T, W] float64, required: the torque (N m) the spin velocity drive applied to the nut about +z over the step that ends at the frame (frame 0: 0), i.e. the engine's applied joint drive torque. Alloy: kd (target - omega) with omega after the step (its implicit velocity actuator)

export.scored_by: Alloy's ThreadA9Twin: record (z, theta), the torque channel from drive_tau, scalars (thread_metrics: advance per rev and mean drive torque over the run-down after 0.25 s)

contact_pairs.note: the friction Alloy's MuJoCo rows use (geom mu mixed by max); Coulomb, static = dynamic, elliptic cone, no torsional / rolling friction, no restitution (MuJoCo soft contact)

fit.note: 6g/6H: the bolt's diameters sit `clearance` below the nut's; normal to a 60 deg flank that is clearance / 4. OBJ-to-OBJ gaps include the facet sag of the other mesh
